subject: Deliver local project skill installation
description:
## Capability

Deliver the approved Bun-native Effect CLI that synchronizes selected source skills into a target project as transaction-safe local agent instructions.

## Final acceptance criteria

- [ ] `agent-skills add [target]` and its native `install` alias satisfy the complete product, filesystem, recovery, and output contract.
- [ ] All 20 numbered product acceptance criteria have direct evidence.
- [ ] All required pure, scoped-filesystem, CLI-runner, and real-process tests pass.
- [ ] The repository remains one private package and `bun run check` passes.

## Source

- `specs/local-project-skills-cli.md`, sections “Purpose,” “Goals,” and “Acceptance criteria” 1–20.
- `specs/ticket-planning.md`, sections “Hierarchy” and “Coverage contract.”
context:
## Shared product context

- Use the specification terms source repository, source skill, stable skill, draft skill, target project, managed skill, unmanaged collision, and included source entry.
- The registry is the ownership authority; generated skill directories are replaceable state.
- Full cross-file atomicity is provided by staging, a durable journal, rollback/recovery, and registry-last ownership commit.
- `install` is an alias of the same `add` command value and handler.

## Child map

- Package bootstrap.
- `add` selector, registry, planning, recovery, synchronization, drift/removal, and failure packets.
- Final CLI-runner and process qualification.

subject: Bootstrap the private Bun Effect package
description:
## Outcome

Create a green private single-package Bun and Effect delivery boundary with an importable runner and executable edge.

## In scope

- Pin Bun, Effect RC, platform-bun, YAML, TypeScript, Vitest, OxLint, and OxFmt versions and create `bun.lock`.
- Add the required strict solution/source/test/tools TypeScript projects, scripts, package exports, Bun shebang, and minimal `src/main.ts` runner seam.
- Adapt the referenced Effect lint presets, warnings-denied rules, formatting exclusions, and Vitest setup.
- Add only compilation, import, and process-entry smoke evidence.

## Out of scope

- The final `add` command tree, prompt, help contract, or alias behavior.
- Catalog, registry, planner, installer, transaction, routing, or Git-ignore behavior.
- Workspaces, `packages/`, Node runtime support, or publish mappings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bun install` creates the pinned lockfile and the root is one private ESM package.
- [ ] Source emits JavaScript, declarations, declaration maps, and source maps under `dist/`.
- [ ] The Bun entrypoint and exported runner can be loaded through a disposable process smoke test.
- [ ] Focused verification and `bun run check` pass.

## Source

- `specs/local-project-skills-cli.md`, sections “Package and tooling setup,” “Package entrypoints,” “Scripts,” “TypeScript configuration,” “OxLint and OxFmt,” and “Vitest.”
- `specs/local-project-skills-cli.md`, process-level smoke requirement and acceptance criteria 1, 2, and 20.

- [ ] Planning and preflight finish before mutation.
- [ ] Startup recovery always precedes ordinary registry, catalog, prompt, and collision handling.
- [ ] Installation, no-op, refresh, removal, rollback, and typed failure behavior satisfy acceptance criteria 3–19.

subject: Present a fully validated skill selector
description:
## Outcome

Expose `add` and its native `install` alias only after the complete source catalog and target have been validated safely.

## In scope

- Add the minimal Effect command tree, native alias, optional directory argument, cwd default, normalized absolute target, and explicit module-relative source-root capability.
- Discover every non-hidden `SKILL.md`, decode YAML with a real parser, classify and sort stable/draft skills, and render complete descriptions.
- Validate all catalog entries before prompting, including unselected skills, duplicate identities, name mismatch, containment, marker-bearing descriptions, and included symlinks.
- Permit quit and first-run zero selection without target mutation.

## Out of scope

- Registry decoding and existing-selection preselection.
- Synchronization planning or target-file mutation.
- Final help/output/process qualification.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `add` and `install` reach the same command value and handler, and the selector labels stable and draft skills deterministically.
- [ ] Invalid catalog or source-root state returns its typed failure before the prompt is invoked.
- [ ] Omitted and supplied targets resolve to one normalized existing directory; invalid targets fail without project mutation.
- [ ] Quit and zero selection leave target sentinels byte-identical.
- [ ] Focused verification and `bun run check` pass.

## Source

- `specs/local-project-skills-cli.md`, sections “Commands,” “Target argument,” “Interactive selection,” “Source repository resolution,” and “Skill discovery and validation.”
- Pure test bullets for metadata, classification, marker descriptions, and duplicates; CLI test bullets for alias, labels, target, and quit.
- Acceptance criteria 3–5, 9, and source/catalog portions of 17.

subject: Preselect registry-owned skills
description:
## Outcome

Decode versioned target ownership and preselect current managed skill names without treating malformed state as empty.

- Preselect choices by stable skill name; omit retired source names from choices.
- Establish deterministic skill-name ordering and exact two-space/trailing-newline registry encoding.

## Out of scope

- Source digest calculation from toolbox entries.
- Routing, Git-ignore, destination-tree, or synchronization planning.
- Registry writes or target mutation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing owned names are preselected and submitted selection is treated as complete desired state.
- [ ] Missing registry is empty state, while invalid or unsupported registry state fails before prompting.
- [ ] Registry codec tests prove deterministic ordering, encoding, and digest syntax validation.
- [ ] Focused verification and `bun run check` pass.

subject: Plan exact synchronization bytes
description:
## Outcome

- Strip frontmatter only from the copied entrypoint while preserving body bytes, line endings, nested files, and relative structure.
- Render deterministic registry bytes, complete-description routing bytes, and idempotent Git-ignore bytes.
- Cover pure plans for install, refresh, no-op, removal, category move, name change, and retired source.

## Out of scope

- Target ownership/path conflict rejection.
- Transaction staging, journal creation, or target mutation.
- Actual refresh, no-op, or removal execution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One public planning behavior returns complete intended operations and exact bytes without creating a transaction directory.
- [ ] Entrypoint-only frontmatter removal and nested body/line-ending preservation are exact.
- [ ] Routing insertion/replacement/removal/idempotency and Git-ignore equivalence/newline rules are proven.
- [ ] All desired-state classifications from the pure test strategy are covered.
- [ ] Focused verification and `bun run check` pass.

subject: Reject target ownership conflicts

subject: Recover valid pending transactions
description:
## Outcome

Restore an uncommitted valid transaction or finalize a committed valid transaction before ordinary synchronization begins.

## In scope

- Introduce the versioned Schema-decoded journal, registry-byte hashes, normalized closed path set, backups, and shared restore operation.
- Restore previous managed directories, text files, and registry when next-registry ownership was not committed.
- Keep the new state and remove only transaction evidence when current registry bytes match the journal’s next hash.
- Recover interrupted newly created destinations before unmanaged-collision classification.

## Out of scope

- The exhaustive malformed/unsafe journal matrix.
- Injected restore or finalization failures.
- Ordinary synchronization mutation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A valid uncommitted fixture restores exact prior bytes and removes newly created paths.
- [ ] A committed-next-registry fixture retains new state and removes the transaction area.
- [ ] Operation evidence proves recovery precedes catalog discovery, registry decoding, prompting, and collision checks.
- [ ] Focused verification and `bun run check` pass.

## Source

- `specs/local-project-skills-cli.md`, sections “Durable transaction area,” “Startup recovery,” and synchronization phase 2.
- Filesystem tests for interrupted new installs and committed-next-registry finalization.
- Acceptance criterion 19 recovery portion.

subject: Reject unsafe transaction journals
description:
## Outcome

Fail closed on missing, malformed, ambiguous, or path-unsafe transaction journals without recovery mutation.

## In scope

- Reject absent or duplicate journal state, invalid JSON/schema/version/hash data, and inconsistent operation metadata.
- Reject absolute, escaping, duplicate, out-of-set, or otherwise unsafe journal paths.
- Reject symlink hazards in the transaction evidence or recovery path.
- Preserve the transaction area and all target sentinels for diagnosis.

## Out of scope

- Valid-journal restore/finalization behavior.
- I/O failure while executing an otherwise valid recovery.
- Ordinary synchronization or rollback-failure reporting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every malformed or unsafe fixture returns `TransactionJournalMalformed`.
- [ ] No recovery or ordinary synchronization mutation occurs.
- [ ] Competing malformed registry/catalog state cannot outrank journal validation.
- [ ] Focused verification and `bun run check` pass.

## Source

- `specs/local-project-skills-cli.md`, sections “Durable transaction area,” “Startup recovery,” and `TransactionJournalMalformed`.

subject: Contain transaction recovery failures
description:
## Outcome

- Preserve the valid journal and required backups whenever cleanup would destroy restart evidence.

- Malformed journals.
- Cooperative rollback during ordinary application.
- Failure of rollback itself.

- [ ] Each valid-journal recovery failure is reported as `TransactionRecoveryFailed`.
- [ ] Recoverable evidence remains intact.
- [ ] Competing invalid catalog or registry state does not outrank recovery failure.
- [ ] Focused verification and `bun run check` pass.

subject: Install selected skills transactionally
description:
## Outcome

Synchronize selected skills into a fresh target using complete staging, durable journaling, cooperative rollback, and registry-last ownership commit.

## In scope

- Build complete staged toolboxes and backups before replacement; durably write a valid journal before the first target replacement.
- Copy all non-hidden regular files/directories, preserve bytes and executable state, strip only entrypoint frontmatter, and leave source skills unchanged.
- Create or update routing and Git-ignore files, apply the plan, write the registry last, clean safely, and emit a concise receipt.
- Include one deterministic application failure proving baseline cooperative rollback through the shared recovery operation.

## Out of scope

- Managed refresh, destination drift, exact no-op, or deselection.
- Exhaustive application-failure and rollback matrices.
- Rollback failure or final CLI/process qualification.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A selected skill installs with its full nested toolbox and correct target text/registry files.
- [ ] Hidden entries are absent, executable files remain executable, and source/nested files remain unchanged.
- [ ] Journal-before-replacement, complete-tree replacement, registry-last commit, and safe cleanup are proven.
- [ ] A representative expected failure restores previous target state.
- [ ] Focused verification and `bun run check` pass.

## Source

- `specs/local-project-skills-cli.md`, sections “Copy and synchronization semantics” and “Planning, staging, and failure safety.”
- Synchronization phases 8–12 and filesystem tests for copy shape, bytes, permissions, registry-last, cleanup, and injected rollback.
- Acceptance criteria 7–13, 18, and 19.

subject: Report exact managed no-ops
description:

- Drift replacement mechanics already owned by the refresh Ticket.
- Removal behavior.
- Process-level output qualification beyond the focused no-op receipt.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exact matches are not replaced or rewritten.
- [ ] Hidden, extra, wrong-kind, symlink, byte, and executable drift are never misreported as unchanged.
- [ ] Registry and routing bytes remain stable across repeated no-ops.
- [ ] Focused verification and `bun run check` pass.

subject: Restore state after expected failures
description:
## Outcome

Map expected filesystem failures precisely and restore prior state across installation, refresh, and removal operations.

## In scope

- Map representative read, write, copy, and executable-permission failures to their distinct typed failures with useful paths and platform reasons.
- Inject failures before journaling, after journaling, between replacements, before registry commit, and during registry replacement.
- Restore prior managed directories, routing, Git-ignore, and registry after cooperative application failures.
- Clean transaction evidence only after successful rollback; preserve it when cleanup would destroy recovery evidence.

## Out of scope

- Failure of the rollback operation itself.
- Malformed or startup-recovery journal failures.
- New synchronization success behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `FileReadFailed`, `FileWriteFailed`, `FileCopyFailed`, and `PermissionUpdateFailed` retain actionable reason information.
- [ ] Every cooperative post-journal application failure restores exact prior state and previous registry authority.
- [ ] Successful rollback cleans staging/backups; unsafe cleanup leaves recoverable evidence.
- [ ] Focused verification and `bun run check` pass.

## Source

- `specs/local-project-skills-cli.md`, sections “Application requirements” and “Typed failures.”
- Filesystem tests for injected expected failure, rollback, cleanup, and registry-last ordering.

subject: Preserve evidence after rollback failure

## Outcome
